title: Node health card still prints the player-facing label "STRAINED" while the ruling renames strain->congestion
detail: The only old-vocabulary word on a + line in the entire diff. The function's own type and color were renamed (Congestion_Level, state_congested) and the HUD legend now reads "node congestion", yet the inspect card's Amber label keeps the banned word; the lane two-tier carve-out does not cover strain.
recommended_fix: Rename the returned label to "CONGESTED" (e.g. return "CONGESTED", p.state_congested, "!") to match the congestion vocabulary used everywhere else.

title: validate_set_emphasis / apply_set_emphasis proc names keep the old command word while their parameter type was renamed to Cmd_Set_Weights
detail: The command Cmd_Set_Emphasis was renamed to Cmd_Set_Weights everywhere (types.odin, serialize.odin, qos_panel.odin, qos_test.odin, harness), but these two core procs keep "set_emphasis" in their identifiers on the very lines that rename the type. Unless the audit scope column exempts them, this is an un-documented exception.
recommended_fix: Rename to validate_set_weights / apply_set_weights, updating the two call sites in topology_apply_edit.

title: E22 drop concept still called "the spawn-side ladder" in the Balance struct comment directly below the renamed E9 "drop precedence" comment
evidence:
-	lane_queue_packets: i32, // E9: a lane queue sheds (drop ladder) at this depth
+	lane_queue_packets: i32, // E9: a lane queue sheds (drop precedence) at this depth
 	pool_max_packets:   i32, // E22: in-flight cap; the spawn-side ladder drops at this depth
detail: The ruling renames drop ladder->drop precedence; flow.odin renamed the same E22 mechanism to "the drop precedence engages over the pool". This adjacent line in the same struct still calls the E22 drop "the spawn-side ladder" — a sweep residue.
recommended_fix: Update the comment to "E22: in-flight cap; the spawn-side drop precedence sheds at this depth" (or similar, dropping the word ladder).

title: crisis.odin still refers to the drop mechanism as "the ladder" in two comments adjacent to renamed "drop precedence" lines
detail: Each "drop precedence" rename in this file is immediately followed by an unchanged context line still calling the drop mechanism "the ladder" ("the ladder just shed", "the ladder's own measure"). Same concept, mixed vocabulary within the same comment block.
recommended_fix: Rename the surviving mentions: "(the drop precedence just shed)" and "— the drop precedence's own measure".

title: qos_test.odin keeps "E22 pool-exhaustion ladder" and "the full ladder" for the drop mechanism while renaming the adjacent E9 mention
detail: The E9 mention on the prior line was renamed to "drop precedence" and the test renamed test_qos_drop_precedence_e9, but the unchanged next line ("E22 pool-exhaustion ladder") and the renamed test's own comment ("the full ladder") retain the old drop-ladder vocabulary.
recommended_fix: Update both comments to "drop precedence": "the E22 pool-exhaustion drop precedence" and "E9 — the full drop precedence, every emptiness combo".

title: flow.odin retains "the E9 contention ladder" and "full ladder BE -> Standard -> Express" after renaming the E9 comment to "contention drop precedence"
detail: Two unchanged context lines in the same function still name the E9 drop mechanism "ladder" ("the E9 contention ladder", "full ladder BE → Standard → Express") while the adjacent comments were renamed to "contention drop precedence" — inconsistent vocabulary in one comment block.
recommended_fix: Rename to "the E9 contention drop precedence" and "full precedence BE → Standard → Express".

title: Mechanical rename produced the doubled word "congested/congested" in the Congestion_Level doc comment
evidence:
+// None = healthy (no telegraph); Amber = congested/congested; Red = critical.
-// None = healthy (no telegraph); Amber = strained/pressured; Red = critical.
detail: The old comment distinguished node (strained) from pipe (pressured); the flat rename collapsed both to "congested", yielding the doubled "congested/congested" — a mechanical-rename prose wart on a live comment.
recommended_fix: Rewrite as "Amber = congested; Red = critical" (or "Amber = congested (node/pipe)") to avoid the doubled word.

title: "congestion" used as a verb in the node_health_test non-vacuous-pin failure message
evidence:
+	testing.expectf(t, any_congested, "the fixture must actually congestion a node (non-vacuous pin)")
-	testing.expectf(t, any_strained, "the fixture must actually strain a node (non-vacuous pin)")
detail: The mechanical rename turned the verb "strain" into the noun "congestion": "must actually congestion a node" is ungrammatical. The message only shows on failure, but it is live test prose.
recommended_fix: Use the verb form: "the fixture must actually congest a node (non-vacuous pin)".

recommended_fix: Use the verb form: "(waiting_ticks 0) never congest, so a healthy busy network emits".
